title: Common component and dimension at a closed fibre interior point
statement: Let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], $f:X\to T$ any scheme morphism, and $z\in Z$. Suppose that the point $f.\operatorname{asFiber}(i(z))$ of the ordinary fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is a generic point [def-sc-generic-point] of an irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] and belongs to the interior of the inverse image of $i(Z)$ in this fibre. Then $z$, as a point of the fibre of $f\circ i$, is generic in an irreducible component of that fibre, and the local topological dimensions [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] of the two fibres at these points are equal.

proof.text: Construct the canonical map of ordinary fibres by pullback.map. Pullback pasting shows that it is a base change of i, hence a closed immersion. Scheme.Pullback.range_map identifies its range with the inverse image of i(Z). The map sends the fibre point of z to the fibre point of i(z).

For a closed embedding j and a point a whose image is component generic, the image of every irreducible set containing closure {a} is contained in closure {j(a)} by component maximality. Closedness identifies the latter closure with the image of closure {a}; injectivity then gives maximality of closure {a}. This is the private, proved component_of_embedding lemma.

For an embedding, preimages of target open neighbourhoods give dim_a(source) <= dim_j(a)(target). In the reverse direction, represent a source open as a preimage of a target open, intersect the target open with the interior of the range, and compare dimensions via the embedding onto its range. This proves the private local_dimension_eq_of_embedding_interior lemma without any sorry. Apply it to the closed fibre immersion.

theorem common_fibre_component_dimension_of_mem_interior
    {Z X T : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ T) (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (z : Z)
    (hinterior : f.asFiber (i z) ∈
      interior ((f.fiberι (f (i z))) ⁻¹' Set.range i))
    (hcomponent : f.asFiber (i z) ∈ genericPoints (f.fiber (f (i z)))) :
    (i ≫ f).asFiber z ∈ genericPoints ((i ≫ f).fiber ((i ≫ f) z)) ∧
      topologicalKrullDimAt ((i ≫ f).asFiber z) =
        topologicalKrullDimAt (f.asFiber (i z))
